prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Boundary: offshore/shore wind-farm O&M; excludes public grid/unrelated port operations. Aliases: Glassfin=Turbine Controller; Morrowick=Offshore Substation; Pale Lantern=Weather Service; Juniper Vale=SCADA Gateway; Thistle Crown=Maintenance Planning Engine; Amber Quay=Shore Control Room; Kestrel Bay=Crew Transfer Vessel; Sable Orchard=Fleet Dispatch Console; Mosslight=Warehouse System; Copper Finch=Metocean Buoy; Quiet Harbor=Cybersecurity Gateway; Blue Granite=Vessel AIS Receiver; Larkspur=Blade Inspection Drone; Redoubt=Work Permit Portal; Foxglove=Emergency Generator; Wildmere=Grid Interface Relay. Elements: Pitch System/Converter Cabinet/Nacelle Condition Monitor/Rotor Brake Unit/Turbine Sensor Bus/Main Transformer/Export Cable Monitor/Spares Hub/Helideck/Daughter Craft/Service Operations Vessel. Flows: Glassfin→Pitch Deviation Notice→Juniper Vale; gateway: work-package flags/Session Revocation Receipt/status. Mosslight→Backorder Exception Slip→Storekeeper(validation). Duty Planner→Transfer Manifest Addendum→Field Supervisor/Thistle Crown/Vessel Master(predeparture). Blue Granite→timestamps/Position Quality Flag/positions→Marine Coordinator/Sable Orchard. Copper Finch→Wave Burst Record/seas/offline logs; Pale Lantern→Squall Window Bulletin/forecasts/confidence; Morrowick→requested Transformer Tap Snapshot; Thistle Crown→Deferred Task Rationale(non-safety). Turbine Sensor Bus collects Glassfin/Pitch System/Converter Cabinet/Nacelle Condition Monitor measurements; Juniper Vale→timestamped observations→Amber Quay; retain source/time/turbine identifier. Condition/cable evidence→planning; validated conditions→Thistle Crown. Weather/buoy contextualize deterioration. Requirements: Duty Planner verifies urgency/feasibility/access/parts/competence/duration; safety/generation-loss precede inspections; justify outages; schedule long-lead work early; update/communicate executable priorities after changes/delays/cancellations/access alternatives. Field Supervisor validates; dispatch assigns approved resources. Weather Analyst compares observations/forecasts; confidence cannot replace limits. Weather Hold blocks unsafe/unsupported work; forecast improvement alone insufficient. Vessel Standby permits transit/station-keeping,not unjustified work/transfers. Marine Coordinator distributes/reassesses plans/routes/forecasts; Vessel Master approves/may abort transfers. Reassess ongoing work near limits; withdraw inadequate-margin personnel. Record

New part:
S311: Inspection findings are compared with the original observations before the alert is closed or converted into corrective work.
S312: The Crew Transfer Vessel uses the Harness Audit Card to verify the applicable equipment checks before personnel transfer.
S313: The Blade Inspection Drone produces the Leading Edge Tile Image during a close-range survey of the blade surface.
S314: Larkspur shall repeat a close-range pass when image coverage is insufficient to assess the suspected surface condition.
S315: The Blade Specialist reviews available inspection evidence and reports whether further examination is warranted.
S316: The Control Engineer reassesses the alert after field findings or corrected sensor data become available.
S317: The Shore Control Room retains the decision record, supporting observations, and response outcome for operational review.
S318: Permit controls coordinate approved work scope, electrical isolation, field execution, and return to service without treating authorization as proof of a safe electrical state.
S319: The Duty Planner submits a defined task scope, work location, crew, and requested operating window for review.
S320: The Field Supervisor confirms that the proposed method, access arrangements, and work party are suitable for the task.
S321: Redoubt shall block permit release until required risk reviews and isolation references are complete.
S322: The HSE Officer reviews task hazards and confirms that required controls are assigned before the permit is authorized.
S323: The Weather Analyst uses the Wave Burst Record to assess whether the planned access period remains suitable.
S324: The Port Agent issues the Berth Slot Confirmation for the planned work period.
S325: The Electrical Technician identifies the electrical sources, isolation points, and verification steps required by the approved scope.
S326: The Substation Operator applies authorized switching actions and records the resulting equipment state.
S327: For turbine work, the Electrical Technician verifies the relevant local isolation and secures the equipment against unintended energization.
S328: Turbine Lockout is maintained while personnel are exposed to the identified hazards.
S329: Work begins only after the Field Supervisor confirms that the permit is active and the required isolations have been independently verified.
S330: The Field Supervisor briefs the crew on the permit limits, isolation boundaries, communications, and conditions requiring work to stop.
S331: The Electrical Technician proves the test instrument, tests for absence of voltage, and proves the instrument again where the procedure requires it.
S332: The Personnel Tracking Console supports confirmation that personnel assigned to the task are accounted for at the work location.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
